text:
adele: quick sketch: 'reserve bands' + burst-token wallet + fast prewarm option. thoughts?
tom: sketch looks good. what are bands?
chris: prefer numeric example for procurement.
rachel: sales: need sample invoice row and SLA bullets.
adele: draft bands: Band 1 - 12 GPUs baseline + 35% burst; Band 2 - 36 GPUs baseline + 22% burst; Band 3 - 120 GPUs baseline + 12% burst. burst expressed as gpu-minutes ledger, tracked per-region.
tom: autoscale behaviour: while tenant has burst -> allow instant scale-up up to baseline+burst. when burst exhausted -> cap at baseline, route excess to shared pool and degrade to lighter model variant. downscale cooldown 8-12m to avoid thrash.
chris: telemetry needs: tenant.burst_remaining, tenant.burst_used, tenant.baseline_usage, tenant.fallback_count; include routing.trace tag commit_band and commit_id.
rachel: pilot asks: 7-day burst top-up for testing, and a one-time prewarm (max 3h) on upgrades. billing: soft-proration window 48h on band changes; no automatic refunds unless SLA breach.
adele: launch checklist (draft): 1) API + DB migration for tenant commit fields 2) Console panels + invoice examples 3) Autoscale + fallback chaos tests 4) Pilot with 3 customers (one per band) 5) Legal & finance sign-off 6) Canary -> GA.
ops-bot: chaos test scheduled Friday 02:00 UTC; canary deploy tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
tom: dev estimate: migration + routing + billing hooks ~3 sprints.
chris: infra estimate: telemetry + autoscale tuning ~2 sprints in parallel.
rachel: i'll prepare customer one-pager and invoice templates for procurement.
adele: I'll author RFC tonight including commit-band definitions, API contract, billing examples, telemetry spec, oncall playbook, and chaos scenarios. tagging owners shortly. :thumbsup:
